title: Converge the real-money rosters on the finished corpus — rule registered BEFORE the numbers land
note: OPERATOR DIRECTIVE 2026-09-22, verbatim: 'there does need to be some convergence here... the state is still representing something that's incorrect, so either the bybit or the breakout accounts need to have the correct adjustments based on the results we see from running those tests.' AGREED. [!] THE INCOHERENCE IS NOT WHAT IT LOOKS LIKE. It is not that prop carries a leg bybit_2 lacks. MEASURED 2026-09-22 over the 30 Bybit-tradeable legs (symbols ending USDT) in config/strategies.yaml: only 9 carry a decision-rule verdict (5 pass, 4 fail); 21 HAVE NEVER BEEN GRADED. The roster reflects HISTORY, not evidence; the prop/bybit asymmetry is a symptom, not the disease. [!] A NAIVE RULE WOULD BE ACTIVELY DANGEROUS, which is why the operator has to set the second half. The 30 legs are 4 families and ONE family is 11 of them: trend_donchian on BTC, ADA, AVAX, ETH x3, SOL x3, XRP. If costs-on leaves most of those positive, `everything that clears the bar goes on the real-money roster` puts THE SAME SIGNAL on up to 7 correlated alts at risk_pct 0.015 each -- ~10% of the book on one strategy, which is one bet sized 9x, not diversification. The pullback family has the same shape (ada +21.58, xrp +16.41, avax +15.68, sol +8.78 pre-cost) AND its ETH member GRADED FAIL. So clearing the bar is NECESSARY AND NOT SUFFICIENT, and the missing half is a per-family / correlation budget. [!] PROP SHOULD NOT CONVERGE TO THE SAME SET AS BYBIT: breakout_1 is bound by the prop firm's account-killer limits (daily-loss $150, static-DD floor $300), which cap concurrent risk units far below bybit_2. The operator's own framing was right -- prop as a SUBSET is expected; prop carrying what bybit_2 lacks is what needed explaining. [!] MIRROR CONSTRAINT, NON-NEGOTIABLE: bybit_portfolio mirrors bybit_2 EXACTLY (tests/test_paper_portfolio_accounts.py asserts ORDERED equality on strategies AND symbols), so every roster edit lands in ONE commit covering both; that mirror is Gate 2's demotion signal. [!] AND THERE IS NO MECHANISM: config/mandates.yaml is ABSENT from origin/main (verified with git cat-file), B5 is `queued` and unbuilt, and scripts/ops/render_daily_brief.py says so already -- 'today: absent -- B5 is not built'. CLAUDE.md's 'THE LADDER IS FULLY AUTOMATED' is an operator GRANT, not a built fact. Until B5 lands every convergence is a manual Tier-3 decision, which is exactly the loop this row sits in. [!] SUPERSEDED IN PART, SAME DAY, BY B6 -- READ B6 BEFORE ACTING ON THIS ROW. The operator answered R8's concentration question `No cap -- everything that passes runs`, and that answer STANDS for bybit_2. But they then reframed the PROP half entirely: prop is not a risk-avoidance problem, it is an EXPECTED-VALUE bet -- `it's ok if there is ever breach... we want to promote strategies that create a portfolio that we would statistically expect to produce a profit (over the initial account cost of about 1%) before the account dies`. So breakout_1 does NOT converge to a subset of bybit_2 chosen by the same criterion: its selection maximises P(reaching the profit target before the drawdown floor), which is not the same ordering as net_R. B6 carries that bar and the missing measurement it needs. [!] AND THE CORRELATION POSITION IS DELIBERATELY ASYMMETRIC ACROSS THE TWO BOOKS, which is worth stating so nobody `harmonises` it later: no concentration cap on bybit_2 (operator's explicit choice), while on prop uncorrelated drawdowns are LOAD-BEARING -- not as a risk limit but as the mechanism that raises P(survival to target). Same input, opposite roles. [!] R8's bybit_2 half remains as written and still blocks on R7. [!] LANDED 2026-09-22 AS ONE LEG, NOT TWO, AND THE CUT IS THE RECORD WORTH KEEPING. Staged: ada_pullback_2h + avax_pullback_2h onto bybit_2 and its mirror. Merged: ada_pullback_2h ONLY. THE MANAGER SELECTED CANDIDATES ON A FOLD **COUNT** ('3/4 or 4/4 positive') AND NEVER READ WHICH FOLD WAS NEGATIVE. From the committed fold_detail, in time order: ada +8.87 -> +2.72 -> +6.84 -> +3.51 (4/4, most recent POSITIVE, +13.06R excluding the oldest fold); avax +15.39 -> +1.10 -> +0.54 -> -4.36 (whole pooled result is fold 1 a year old; last nine months -2.72R; last quarter -4.36R over 12 trades). fade_breakout_4h and htf_pullback_trend_2h have the SAME shape. All three 3/4 legs are negative in their MOST RECENT fold — the count concealed exactly the thing that decides. [!] AND THE DISCHARGE ARGUMENT FOR avax WAS WRONG ON ITS OWN TERMS. The manager argued the 2026-07-22 demotion set its own re-promotion condition ('a 4-6wk shadow re-eval is expected') and that +12.6729R over n=45 met it. The demotion is dated 2026-07-22; the corpus's fold 4 runs 2026-07-09 -> 2026-09-20. THE RE-EVAL *IS* FOLD 4, and fold 4 is -4.3601R. The pooled figure was discharged against ten months that PREDATE the demotion. The demotion therefore STANDS, undischarged. [!] OPERATOR 2026-09-22: 'wire ada only and send avax to the research que for refinement' and, on whether to add a recency clause to RULE-D1, 'Route it to research first'. Filed as RQ-20260922-013 (avax refinement, with a KILL proposal as the declared outcome if no grid variant clears the recent window) and RQ-20260922-012 (fold recency across the whole corpus).
